reading.body:
The operator publishes only floor area for this facility: 759,000 square feet of technical space. No power consumption, critical power capacity, or uptime certification appears in the structured data available, making it impossible to estimate compute density or reliability tier.

Floor area alone does not indicate AI workload suitability. Data centers vary widely in power delivery per square foot, cooling architecture, and electrical redundancy. A large floor footprint with low power density serves different purposes than a compact facility engineered for high-density compute. Without a megawatt figure, this facility's role in the AI infrastructure stack cannot be determined from what is published.

Colorado publishes power figures for only one of its seventeen mapped facilities in this dataset, totaling 18 MW statewide. This absence of power disclosure across most facilities limits visibility into the state's actual compute capacity and growth trajectory. Operators' own pages often omit technical specifications that would indicate suitability for intensive workloads, leaving floor area as a proxy measure that does not reliably predict AI infrastructure value.
